summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, diastolic heart failure, alcoholic cirrhosis, and recent gastrointestinal bleeding presented with a single episode of bright red blood per rectum and a significantly low hemoglobin. She was admitted for management of acute posthemorrhagic anemia and received three units of packed red blood cells. Evaluation revealed internal hemorrhoids and diverticulosis as the likely source of bleeding, with no active Crohn’s disease. An EGD showed gastric ulcers, and she was started on pantoprazole. Clopidogrel was held and aspirin dose reduced due to bleeding risk. Her condition stabilized, hemoglobin improved, and she was discharged home in good condition with follow-up plans and medication adjustments.
problems: Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
